centralLane.description: Runs straight down the center between the two wooden posts.

sittingSquares.description: Formed at each intersection of central lane and cross lane. 8 chasers sit in alternate directions.

freeZones.description: D-shaped or rectangular safe turning zone behind each wooden post where chasers may change running direction.

posts.material: Smooth cylindrical teak or metal post without sharp edges

coreMechanics.title: Strict Direction Rule
coreMechanics.summary: Once an active chaser chooses a direction from a post or cross-lane, they MUST continue running in that direction until they reach the opposite free zone post. Reversing direction mid-lane is an immediate foul.
coreMechanics.foulPenalty: Umpire blows foul whistle; chaser must yield advantage or hand over Kho correctly.

coreMechanics.title: Central Lane Barrier
coreMechanics.summary: The active chaser CANNOT step over or cut across the central line dividing the two halves of the court. To switch halves, the chaser must either go around a post in the free zone or tap a teammate with a valid Kho.
coreMechanics.foulPenalty: Invalidated tag; red flash foul alert.

coreMechanics.title: The 'Kho!' Handover
coreMechanics.summary: The active chaser must touch the seated teammate on the back between shoulder and waist and simultaneously utter 'Kho!' loud enough for the umpire and players to hear.

coreMechanics.title: Defender Tagging & Elimination
coreMechanics.summary: A defender is dismissed ('out') if touched by an active chaser's hand without any active foul, or if the defender steps outside the court boundary boundaries.
coreMechanics.foulPenalty: 1 point awarded to the chasing team.

traditional.description: Standard KKFI official rules: 1 point per dismissed defender.

ultimateKhoKho.wazirAdvantage: Wazir is a designated attacker who can sprint in BOTH directions freely along the cross-lanes.
ultimateKhoKho.description: Commercial league format introduced in 2022 to supercharge TV viewership and athletic acrobatic play.
